clue.text: Ability to read what's written on low-cal foods with lots of salt

parts.note: packaging on diet products often carries the trade spelling lite for light
salty talk is racy, risqué and spicy

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek link between reading skills and studying the labels on salty diet snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Literacy is the skill of reading and writing, so it is exactly an ability to read.

clue.text: Child detected in fibs is not exactly truthful, for example

indicators.note: the child is found sitting inside the word for fibs, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: fibs are lies
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A youngster is caught out telling fibs and judged less than honest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example of the figure itself: 'not exactly truthful' is an understatement made by denying the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the rhetorical device of understatement by negating the contrary, as in calling a liar 'not exactly truthful'.

clue.text: Striker regularly dropped for match

indicators.note: every other letter of the word Striker is discarded, starting with the first, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A football forward is left out of the side, as he often is, for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a sporting fixture, as in a cup tie, so it means a match.

clue.text: Surreal novel and gripping free travel book

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the word for free inside them
novel as an adjective means new or unusual, so the letters of Surreal are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear

explanation.surface: A reviewer praises a strange, gripping novel alongside a free travel guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges the letters of Surreal, and 'gripping' sets the word for free inside them. William Cobbett's 1830 book records his journeys on horseback through the English countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural Rides is Cobbett's famous book recording his journeys on horseback through rural England, a classic of travel writing.

clue.text: Easy company, fairly loud and beginning to yell

parts.note: mf, mezzo forte, is the musical marking for moderately loud

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word yell is taken

explanation.surface: A relaxed group of friends gets a bit noisy and starts shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfy is informal for comfortable, and an easy chair or easy manner is a comfortable one.

clue.text: Frenchman fighting dense 'scrubby vegetation around the Med

definitions.meaning: a member of the French Resistance in the Second World War, named after the scrubland where fighters hid
the thick evergreen scrub of Corsica and other Mediterranean coasts

explanation.surface: A French soldier struggles through thick undergrowth on the Mediterranean shore.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for the Mediterranean scrubland also became the name of the wartime Resistance fighters who hid in it.

clue.text: Girl sheltering resistance fighters

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the letter for resistance inside it, as if protecting it

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A young woman hides members of the Resistance from the occupiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a body of soldiers, a large organised force of fighters.

clue.text: Not right if one newspaperman's ragged

parts.note: something not right or not fair is unjust
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
ED is short for editor, a newspaperman

explanation.surface: A complaint that it is unfair when a journalist looks scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragged' is a typesetting term: text set with an uneven right-hand margin is called ragged, or unjustified.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, lines not spaced out to a straight margin are unjustified, which typesetters describe as ragged right.

clue.text: NHS cuts: consult your MP here

definitions.meaning: operations carried out by the National Health Service, Britain's public health system, as surgical cuts
a British Member of Parliament holds sessions where constituents can come and raise problems

explanation.surface: A protest slogan: if the health service is being cut, go and complain to your MP.
explanation.walkthrough: British MPs hold regular local sessions called surgeries where constituents meet them in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery means both operations by a surgeon and an MP's advice session for constituents.

clue.text: Smart dresser in mostly red burgundy finished with silver-grey

indicators.note: all but the last letter of the wine name is used

parts.note: Beaune is a red wine from Burgundy, named after its town
ash is a pale silvery grey colour

explanation.surface: A dandy in a wine-coloured outfit, its trim finished in pale grey.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash (1674-1761) was the master of ceremonies at Bath and a celebrated leader of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard 'Beau' Nash was the famed Georgian dandy who set fashions in Bath society.

clue.text: Initially, Thomas Hardy put one who may flourish in a key novel

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the novelist's two names are taken
with in, this says one piece is placed inside another
with put, this signals placing one piece within the key

parts.note: E major is a musical key
a trumpet sounds a flourish or fanfare, and the word also names its player

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy, the novelist, is imagined writing a fanfare in a musical key.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy supplies the initials TH and is also the author of the novel, so the surface leads straight to the right book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trumpet-Major is an 1880 novel by Thomas Hardy, set during the Napoleonic Wars.

clue.text: Vehicle robustly rebuilt around shell of limousine

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the outside letters of limousine
something rebuilt is put together anew, so the letters of robustly are rearranged
the outer casing of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A car robustly rebuilt around the body of an old limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' looks like a car being restored, but the definition is a general one, and the limousine only lends its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolleybus is an electric bus drawing power from overhead wires, a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Unusually complex manifest filled in with weight estimated

indicators.note: the word for manifest is filled by the other pieces placed within it

parts.note: overt means open, manifest or plain to see
a rough figure is an estimated one

explanation.surface: A shipping manifest is filled in with a cargo weight that was only guessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwrought can describe style that is overelaborate, too ornate and fussy, so unusually complex.

clue.text: An inch is length clung to by English

indicators.note: the English letter attaches itself to the end of the length letter

parts.note: taken as written; that the letters also run unbroken through the clue words is length is a coincidence, as the clue builds them piece by piece

explanation.surface: A tiny unit of measurement that the English cling to rather than going metric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inch' looks like the measurement, but in Scotland an inch is a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: Inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm, so an inch is an isle.

clue.text: Daily dropping front page, backtracking to limit damages

indicators.note: the shortened word is read in the opposite direction
a letter is let fall from the word for a daily newspaper

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper, a paper

indicators.note: only the leading letter of page is the one that goes

parts.note: to ration is to limit supplies

explanation.surface: A daily paper pulls its front-page story and backtracks to limit the damages it must pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is a noun here, a newspaper, not an adverb; 'dropping' removes its first P to leave APER, and 'backtracking' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparation is compensation paid for a wrong, which is what damages awarded in court are.

clue.text: With heroin involved, female dismisses returning officer of county

indicators.note: the drug letter is wrapped up inside the other pieces
the word for dismisses is read backwards

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug scandal: a woman sacks the official who has come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns FIRES into SERIF; F follows, and 'involved' puts H inside after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff is a county official, the chief officer of a shire in England or a county lawman in America.

clue.text: Endless stupidity, with nothing gained, to go back in

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for stupidity is cut off

parts.note: folly is foolishness or stupidity
O looks like zero, nothing
won means gained, as a prize

explanation.surface: Endless foolishness, with nothing gained, to go back in for more.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a side well behind on first innings can be made to follow on: to bat again straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, to follow on is for the batting side to go in again immediately after its first innings.

clue.text: Pleasant feature of friendship — seen regularly to be welcomed

indicators.note: the friendship word takes the other letters in, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: amity is friendship

indicators.note: every other letter of the word seen is taken

explanation.surface: A nice part of friendship is regularly being made welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks E and N from SEEN, and 'to be welcomed' sets them inside AMITY.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a useful or pleasant facility or feature of a place.

clue.text: Pine after conflict over cruel treatment

indicators.note: the wood comes after the reversed piece
in an across clue, over signals the word is turned round

parts.note: war is conflict
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Someone longs for home after a war ends and complains of harsh treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like a verb meaning yearn, but it is the wood: deal is sawn pine or fir.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is unfair or harsh treatment, an idiom for being badly used.

clue.text: Check short measure of red lentils

indicators.note: the colour word is served a little short, losing its final letter

parts.note: lentils are a pulse, the edible seeds of legumes

explanation.surface: A diner checks that they were given a stingy portion of red lentils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short measure of' cuts RED to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to drive it back, to check it.

clue.text: Hard going when line's crowded out and teeming with people

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: the line letter is pushed out of the word for going

parts.note: leaving means going away
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: It's tough leaving when the queue has been squeezed out and the place is packed.
explanation.definitionFit: A heaving place is crammed, so packed with people that it seems to heave.

clue.text: Info on heartless moral principles handed down through the generations

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: an ethic is a set of moral principles

explanation.surface: Information about lost moral values being passed from parent to child.
explanation.walkthrough: ETHIC has the centre letter H, which 'heartless' removes to leave ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic traits are inherited, passed from parents to offspring through the generations.

clue.text: Concert starting on time, though part's cancelled

indicators.note: with cancelled, this says the start was kept even though a piece was removed
the abbreviation for part is struck out, cancelled from the longer word

parts.note: a prompt start is one on time
PT is the abbreviation for part

explanation.surface: A concert begins punctually, though one section is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: A prom is a promenade concert, as at London's summer BBC Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: Prom is short for promenade concert, where some of the audience stand.

clue.text: Cultivated area, so backwards in look with little space

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the word for look

parts.note: regard means look, as in a steady gaze

indicators.note: the word so is read the other way

parts.note: an en is a small printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: A gardener steps back to look at a cultivated plot with a little space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns SO into OS. An en is a printer's measure of space, half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose garden is a cultivated area given over to growing roses.

clue.text: Direction of the Speaker for one in opposition

parts.note: ENE is east-north-east, a compass direction
my means belonging to the person speaking

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker directs a member of the Opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S suggests the Commons Speaker, but 'of the Speaker' just means belonging to whoever is talking.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is an opponent, someone who stands against you.

clue.text: Started giving out good coffee, perhaps

indicators.note: the good letter is given away and leaves the word

parts.note: began means started

explanation.surface: Someone began handing out good coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee is an example of a bean, the seed roasted and ground for the drink.

clue.text: Way to get out of stage door, get-ting outside sooner

indicators.note: the stage and door words go around the outside of the word for sooner

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey
a wicket is a small door or gate set in a larger one
before means sooner

explanation.surface: An actor slips out by the stage door, getting outside early.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'get-ting' is just a line-break hyphen. Leg before wicket is a way a batsman can be dismissed in cricket, when the ball strikes the leg in front of the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, leg before wicket is one of the ways a batsman is given out.

clue.text: Set of parts for Marlowe

definitions.meaning: a collection of pieces for assembly, as in a model
Christopher Marlowe, the Elizabethan playwright, was known by the short form of his first name

explanation.definitionFit: Kit is a set of parts for assembly, and also Christopher Marlowe's familiar first name.

clue.text: European vote a result of canvassing reach?

parts.note: a cross on a ballot paper is a vote
a tent is made of canvas, playing on canvassing for votes

explanation.surface: A European election in which the vote results from door-to-door canvassing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvassing' suggests seeking votes, but here it means covering with canvas, which gives a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent and reach both mean the range or scope that something covers.

clue.text: Sleep-inducing and heady potion out-and-out insomniac used externally

indicators.note: only the outside letters of each of the four words are used

explanation.surface: A heady sleeping draught for a total insomniac, rubbed on the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word gives its first and last letters: HY, PN, OT and IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnotic drugs are those that induce sleep, soporifics.
